counterfactual_missing_items: Immunohistochemistry confirming colonic origin (e.g., CK20/CDX2) is not reported
Total colonoscopy revealed no endoluminal lesion, which would be expected for a typical luminal colorectal primary
decisive_items: Biopsy of the umbilical lesion demonstrated a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma

Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed homogeneously enhancing umbilical tissue growth and irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon measuring approximately 8.3 cm
A 55-year-old man with no significant medical history presented with a 10-month history of spontaneous, progressively painful umbilical discomfort
response.rationale: R4 integrates the umbilical adenocarcinoma biopsy, the painful enlarging umbilical nodule, and the transverse colon thickening on CT, forming the complete Sister Mary Joseph nodule with metastatic colonic adenocarcinoma. C1 is an append-only completion of R4 that adds the histologic grade already present in R4's raw support, so it is a correlated restatement without independent raw evidence. R1 only captures the colonic thickening and misses the umbilical metastasis and biopsy-confirmed adenocarcinoma, making it incomplete and less specific.

rejected.why: R1 identifies only colorectal cancer from the colonic thickening and omits the umbilical nodule, biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma, and the Sister Mary Joseph nodule presentation, so it is incomplete and less diagnostically specific.
